mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not lead to a significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 1% over 3 months do not lead to a significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% does not lead to a significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and potentially higher costs.
failure_condition: If INDPRO YoY < -2% does not lead to a significant negative 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter and CPIAUCSL YoY is above 2%, the combined signal of tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% in a quarter AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: If the combined trigger does not lead to a significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in a month does not lead to a significant positive 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% YoY and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over 3 months, the combined signal of strong housing demand and consumer spending leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY increase > 10% AND RSAFS increase > 1% over 3 months
failure_condition: If the combined trigger does not lead to a significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% does not lead to a significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) or if the Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
